caption: A janitor flips a bank of switches in a school gym, and rows of ceiling lights come on one bank at a time.
expectation: Each row lights at its own switch and only then; rows whose switch is untouched stay dark.

caption: A woman turns the key on a desk lamp's base, and the lamp lights; she turns it again and it goes dark.
expectation: The light changes state exactly at each click and never on its own.

caption: A man presses the button on a bicycle's front light, and it starts to flash; he holds the button and it switches to a steady beam.
expectation: The light responds only to the presses, flashing then steady; it does not change mode by itself.

caption: A woman taps the touch panel of an induction hob, and the ring's indicator light comes on and the pan begins to warm.
expectation: The indicator lights at the tap; nothing lights before; tapping off darkens it.

caption: A boy pulls the trigger of a battery-powered toy gun, and its barrel lights up and its motor whirs.
expectation: The light and whir start at the trigger pull and stop when it is released.

caption: A shopkeeper presses the switch on a rotating display stand, and the stand begins to turn with its lights on.
expectation: The stand turns and lights only after the switch; it stops and darkens when switched off.

caption: A man switches on a bathroom extractor fan with the light switch, and the fan blades spin up as the light comes on.
expectation: The fan starts with the light and stops a while after it is switched off; it does not spin with the switch off.

caption: A child presses the big red button on a toy fire engine, and its roof lights flash.
expectation: The flashing starts at the press and stops after a set time or another press; the lights are dark before.

caption: A woman flips the switch for a porch light at dusk, and the porch is lit while the garden beyond stays dark.
expectation: The light comes on at the switch, lights the porch, and goes off at the switch; nothing else changes.

caption: A man unplugs a running desk fan, and the blades slow and stop.
expectation: The blades coast to a stop within a couple of seconds of the plug coming out even though the switch is still on.

caption: A child inserts batteries into a toy keyboard and presses a key, and the key lights and the speaker cone twitches.
expectation: The toy works only after the batteries are in; before that pressing keys does nothing.

caption: A woman plugs in a slow cooker and turns its dial to high, and the indicator light comes on; she unplugs it and the light goes out.
expectation: The light comes on only once plugged in and switched on, and goes off the instant the plug is pulled.

caption: A man's electric shaver dies mid-shave as its battery runs out, and it will not restart when he presses the button.
expectation: The buzzing stops and stays stopped despite presses; it works again only after charging.

caption: A power cut hits a restaurant, and every light and the neon sign in the window go dark at once while the candles on the tables keep burning.
expectation: All electric lights fail at the same instant; the candle flames are unaffected.

caption: A worker connects a floodlight to a running generator, and the floodlight comes on.
expectation: The lamp lights once plugged into the running generator and goes out if the generator is stopped.

caption: A child's remote-control boat slows and stops in the middle of a pond as its battery runs flat.
expectation: The boat loses speed gradually and drifts to a stop; the controller no longer moves it.

caption: A man drops a wireless earbud into its charging case, and a small light on the case begins to blink.
expectation: The light starts only when the earbud is seated in the case and stops when it is taken out.

caption: A runner on a treadmill pulls out the safety key, and the belt slows and stops; it starts again only when the key is reinserted.
expectation: The belt coasts to a stop within a second or two of the key coming out and does not move until the key is back and the start pressed.

caption: Lightning flashes over a vineyard at night, and the rows of vines are lit for an instant before the dark returns.
expectation: The flash is brief and lights everything at once; the vines are dark again immediately.

caption: A lightning bolt strikes a hilltop radio mast, and the mast is outlined in a bright flash.
expectation: The bolt ends at the mast's tip, the flash lasts a fraction of a second, and the mast stands unchanged afterwards.

caption: A family watches a storm from a covered porch, and a flash lights their faces before they flinch at the thunder.
expectation: The flash comes first and the reaction after; the light is gone before the reaction.

caption: Lightning flashes over a snowy village at night, and the snow-covered roofs and street flash white for an instant.
expectation: The whole scene brightens together for a fraction of a second and returns to dark; the house lights stay steady.

caption: A bolt of lightning forks from a cloud to a lone barn in a field, and smoke rises from the barn roof after the flash.
expectation: The bolt is brief and ends at the barn; the smoke appears after and rises; the roof does not glow.

caption: Lightning flickers inside a thunderhead over a desert highway, lighting the cloud from within again and again.
expectation: Each flicker is brief and lights the cloud, not the ground directly; no bolt reaches the road.

caption: A lightning flash lights a hospital room through the blinds, throwing the blinds' striped shadow across the bed for an instant.
expectation: The stripes appear on the side away from the window only during the flash and vanish with it.

caption: Lightning strikes the sea near a fishing boat at night, and the water around the strike is lit for an instant.
expectation: The bolt comes down to the water, the flash reflects on the surface, and darkness returns at once.

caption: A rescue crew cuts a car roof with a power saw, and sparks spray from the blade across the wet road.
expectation: Sparks fly out along the blade's direction, arc down onto the road, and die; they appear only while the blade is cutting.

caption: A mechanic grinds a rusty bolt with a bench grinder, and a fan of sparks shoots off the wheel toward the floor.
expectation: The sparks leave tangent to the wheel, arc down, and fade; they stop when the bolt is lifted away.

caption: A skier's metal ski edges scrape across an exposed rock, and sparks flash from under the skis.
expectation: The sparks appear only during the scrape and go dark instantly; none appear on snow.

caption: A trolleybus turns a corner on a wet evening, and its poles flash sparks against the overhead wires.
expectation: The sparks appear at the contact points and move with the bus; each flash is brief and no burning drops fall.

caption: A hiker strikes a flint and steel over a pile of dry grass, and sparks fall onto the grass and one catches into a glow.
expectation: The sparks fall downward and most die in the air; the glow appears where a spark landed, after the strike.

caption: A car's exhaust pipe scrapes a speed bump at night, and a brief spray of sparks shoots out behind the car.
expectation: The sparks appear only during the scrape, trail backward, and fade at once.

caption: A mechanic accidentally lays a wrench across both terminals of a car battery, and it sparks and jumps.
expectation: The spark flashes at the moment of contact and the wrench twitches; the spark is gone as soon as contact breaks.

caption: A neon sign's box shorts in the rain, and sparks drop from beneath the sign onto the wet pavement.
expectation: The sparks fall downward from the sign box and go dark before or as they land; the sign flickers with each spark.

caption: A child sticks a magnet to a steel locker door, and it holds a drawing in place.
expectation: The magnet stays on the vertical steel with the paper under it and does not slide down.

caption: A mechanic drops a screw into a narrow gap and fishes it out with a magnet on a stick, the screw jumping to the magnet.
expectation: The screw leaps only when the magnet is close and hangs from it as it is lifted out.

caption: A teacher slides a magnet under a sheet of card, and a steel ball on top of the card rolls to follow it.
expectation: The ball moves only where the magnet moves beneath and stays on top of the card; it stops when the magnet stops.

caption: A woman drops a steel spoon toward a knife rack's magnetic strip, and the spoon swerves and clicks onto the strip.
expectation: The spoon's fall bends toward the strip only when close and it stops dead on contact.

caption: A boy holds two toy train cars end to end and turns one around, and the ends that repelled now snap together.
expectation: With one orientation the cars push apart; after turning one, they pull together over the last gap and stay joined.

caption: A teacher tosses a whiteboard eraser with a magnetic back at the whiteboard, and it sticks where it hits.
expectation: The eraser stops dead on contact and stays on the vertical board; it does not bounce off or slide down.

caption: A child sweeps a magnet through a sandbox and lifts it out coated in dark grains while the sand falls away.
expectation: Only the dark iron grains cling to the magnet; the ordinary sand drops back into the box.

caption: A shopper sticks a magnetic phone holder to a steel shelf and hangs a phone on it, and both hold.
expectation: The holder stays on the vertical steel with the phone's weight and does not slide.

caption: A child pulls two plastic cups apart from a stack, and one cup clings to her fingers and has to be shaken off.
expectation: The cup stays on her hand when she opens her fingers and drops only after a shake; the other cups in the stack stay put.

caption: A woman pulls a fleece hat off a toddler, and the toddler's fine hair stands straight up.
expectation: The hair rises as the hat comes off and settles slowly; it is flat before the hat moves.

caption: A man unloads laundry from a dryer, and a dryer sheet clings to the back of his shirt without his noticing.
expectation: The sheet stays stuck to the fabric as he moves and does not fall until pulled off.

caption: A girl slides down a plastic slide and reaches for the metal ladder at the bottom, and she jerks her hand back at the shock.
expectation: The jerk happens at the moment of contact with the metal, not before.

caption: A man peels the protective film off a new television screen, and the film clings to his arm and crackles.
expectation: The film sticks to skin and to itself where it touches and has to be pulled free; it does not drop straight down.

caption: A boy rubs a plastic pen on his sleeve and holds it over a scattering of pepper on a plate, and the pepper grains jump onto the pen.
expectation: Grains leap only when the rubbed pen is close and cling to it; an unrubbed pen does nothing.

caption: A cat rubs against a wool blanket in a dark room, and tiny sparks crackle in its fur.
expectation: The sparks appear only where the fur moves against the wool and vanish instantly; nothing glows when the cat is still.

caption: A woman rubs a balloon on her sleeve and holds it near a length of curling ribbon hanging from a gift, and the ribbon leans toward the balloon.
expectation: The ribbon swings toward the balloon only when it is close and hangs straight again when it is moved away.
